chapter: Los Angeles, Central Avenue and the Apex
title: Entertainers at the Apex: Henry Starr, Bojangles, Ethel Waters
summary: West Coast entertainers and visiting stars who came to the Apex, including Henry Starr, Bill Robinson, Ethel Waters and Mildred Bailey.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Who were some of the entertainers that worked (inaudible)? the Apex when you were in the band?

Well, most of those entertainers that I could tell you about were people that were just known on the Pacific Coast. Fellas like Henry Starr (PHONETIC), he was a very, very great singer of songs throughout the Hollywood area here and also up in San Francisco for many years. He was a very, very popular man among the motion picture stars, especially the females because he was a very, very handsome man.
Tall, slender. I met him in San Francisco with Duke Ellington.
All I knew was that he was a friend of Duke's. -- I met him with Duke. (inaudible).
You must have met him on his -- yes, well, he's passed, he's passed now. He was a friend of Duke's. But he was a very, very handsome man and --
And as a young man, he was an eye-catcher and he caught all of the eyes and got with all of the eyes. He didn't miss a thing.
What kind of a singer was he? What kind of songs did he sing?

He played the piano and sang whatever kind of songs that you want to hear according to your mood, which a singer in that day and age had to do. You had to be what was called an entertainer, not just a singer. You were an entertainer. Well, that type of guy was -- and then, he would always, when Bojangles Robinson came in town, he would always come by and do his act, strictly because he liked to be a part of the scene. Wherever he was, he would come around. Ethel Waters would come in. She would sing.
Would Bojangles be appearing in a theater?

He'd be appearing somewhere in town, in a picture or theater or something. But we would always know that he was going to be there and we'd play for him right off the top of our heads. Whatever he wanted to play, we'd do those things. Mildred Bailey used to come by when she first came out with Paul Whiteman. She used to come by and sit and sing with us.
